parsed.explanation: The nationwide penal code in force since December 2024 criminalises same-sex conduct with 2–5 years' imprisonment, fixes the offence by birth sex, and can catch trans visitors whose relationships or presentation are read as same-sex or gender-nonconforming. Pre-existing morality/public-indecency enforcement and post-code reports of increased arbitrary arrests, detention and physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression show state-tolerated targeting. No anti-discrimination law or complaint mechanism exists. No trans-specific entry, facility or custody rules are documented, leaving prison placement and enforcement scale uncertain. No death penalty is documented. This sits above the most lethal 0.15 tier but below exclusion-only 0.35 anchors because imprisonment and abuse are documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry or screening rule is documented, but the penal code recognises no affirmed gender and fixes offences by birth sex, so documents or presentation may expose a visitor to perceived same-sex or gender-nonconforming enforcement.
entry_documents.interaction: Border or status checks could feed into the same criminalisation and morality-enforcement system; actual entry practice for trans visitors is unresolved.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Same-sex conduct is punishable by 2–5 years; gender-nonconforming presentation can lead to arrest on perceived same-sex conduct. Post-code reporting records a significant increase in arbitrary arrests, detentions and physical abuse. Prison placement rules are not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest can follow presentation or relationship status; custody conditions and placement for trans detainees remain unresolved.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The penal code applies nationwide with no standing subnational variation, so there is no documented local refuge from national enforcement. Trans-specific facility or custody rules are not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National enforcement operates without documented local variation; facility and detention practice remains unknown.

care_services.exposure: No trans-specific care protections are documented, and no anti-discrimination law covers service provision on gender identity grounds.
care_services.interaction: Without a complaint mechanism, service denial or mistreatment would have no documented domestic remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The military government justified the penal code as defending traditional moral values; the justice minister called homosexuality unnatural. The undefined ban on 'promotion' is broad, and enforcement has targeted gender-nonconforming expression.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing supports expansive enforcement against visible or perceived gender nonconformity, not just same-sex conduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-specific rules for trans visitors are documented. A minor travelling with an adult would face the same national criminalisation and absence of complaint mechanisms. The family-code adoption ban is resident-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: No guardian or minor-specific protection is documented; general criminalisation and enforcement apply.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Reporting records a significant increase in physical abuse directed at individuals on the basis of appearance or gender expression alone, alongside arbitrary arrests. No anti-discrimination law or protection body exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims have no documented domestic complaint mechanism, and police are implicated as enforcers rather than protectors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, protection body or legal footing for organised advocacy is documented. The scale of arbitrary arrests is described only qualitatively.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of remedy means enforcement exposure is unremediated; unknowns include prison placement and entry practice for trans visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: More severe than this dossier: 0.15-A documents routine visitor arrests, months of pretrial custody, beatings, and a capital pathway. This dossier has statutory 2–5 year imprisonment and reported abuse but no documented execution or capital case, so it sits above 0.15-A.

Less severe than this dossier: 0.25-A involves raids, fines, photographs and rare imprisonment, with execution not imposed. Here imprisonment is statutory for perceived same-sex conduct and post-code arbitrary arrests and abuse increased, so the rating sits below 0.25-A.

Materially below 0.35-A: that anchor is exclusion and humiliation without criminal charge. This dossier documents criminal imprisonment, arbitrary detention and physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression, so it is more severe.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is nationwide criminalisation enforced by a military government framing homosexuality as immoral. The statute imposes 2–5 years and can reach trans visitors through birth-sex classification or gender-nonconforming presentation; reporting documents increased arbitrary arrests, detention and physical abuse since it took effect. No anti-discrimination law or complaint mechanism exists. No trans-specific border, facility or custody rule is documented, but absence of evidence is not safety. The rating is below 0.35 exclusion anchors because imprisonment and abuse are documented, and above 0.15 because no capital or lethal pathway is documented.
